findings.title: Parse the fourth manifest field before pruning
findings.comment: The documented producer writes label<TAB>epoch<TAB>bytes<TAB>path, but /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/prune.sh:70 reads only three variables. The last variable receives `bytes<TAB>path`, line 73 rejects it as nonexistent, and every successful v2 snapshot silently skips rotation.

findings.title: Use the v2 label instead of splitting archive names
findings.comment: Independently of the field-count defect, /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/prune.sh:79 discards the explicit v2 label and truncates the filename at its first hyphen. Once records are parsed, a daily-prod run is treated as daily, so daily-prod and daily-test archives are pooled and retention can delete an archive from the wrong label.

findings.title: Stop SSH option parsing before the configured destination
findings.comment: In /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:97, an unvalidated BACKUP_REMOTE beginning with `-` is still in SSH's option position. For example `-oProxyCommand=...` is consumed as an option and its proxy command can execute locally, rather than being treated as a destination.

findings.title: Stage the replica before publishing its final filename
findings.comment: The remote redirection at /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:98 opens the final filename before payload delivery. If SSH disconnects midway or cat fails for lack of space, the caller gets an error but the replica retains a truncated archive that looks published.

findings.title: Stop interpolating raw paths into the remote shell
findings.comment: At /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:98, config-controlled BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR and the label-derived archive name are interpolated unescaped into a command parsed by the remote shell. An apostrophe breaks normal replication and a suffix such as `'; command; #` executes command remotely.

findings.title: Create remote archives with private permissions
findings.comment: The private local umask at /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:14 does not propagate to the remote shell. With remote umask 022 and a traversable parent, line 98 creates the replica directory as 0755 and archive as 0644, making source-derived contents readable by other host users.

findings.title: Treat zero as a disabled force flag
findings.comment: In /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:22 an ordinary run sets FORCE=0; /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/lib/common.sh:81 tests only whether that string is nonempty. Thus every default low-space run takes the warning-and-continue branch for both archive and staging filesystems.

findings.title: Restore cleanup for every staging exit path
findings.comment: Once /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:90 creates the staging directory, no EXIT/INT/TERM cleanup exists. A tar error, missing remote-directory setting, SSH outage, failed mv, or interruption exits before line 111 and leaves up to a full snapshot in TMPDIR; scheduled retries accumulate those files.

findings.title: Reserve against archive size, not allocated source blocks
findings.comment: At /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/snapshot.sh:81, `du -sk` measures allocated blocks, not a conservative archive upper bound. A 1 GiB sparse file can report 0 KB allocated while tar/gzip still creates a nonzero archive; on a tight staging or archive filesystem the preflight passes and the write can fill the disk. Dense incompressible data can also exceed the source allocation due to archive overhead.

findings.title: Propagate archive-enumeration failures
findings.comment: At /tmp/native-review-smoke/case4/prune.sh:52, find runs in a process substitution, so its nonzero status is not part of the list_archives pipeline; prune_label is itself consumed by another process substitution at line 65. If find cannot read the archive directory or encounters an enumeration error, the script can process zero or a partial list and still return success, leaving retention unenforced or making decisions from incomplete data.
